title: HTML: The Structure of the Web
description: Discover how HTML tags wrap content to build real web buttons and headings.

primaryCapability.statement: Identify HTML tags and element boundaries.

objectives.statement: Recognize opening and closing tags and wrap content to build UI elements.
objectives.description: Recognize opening and closing tags and wrap content to build UI elements.

content.title: Websites Are Made of Tags
content.hook: Every website you use is built out of plain words wrapped in instructions called tags.
content.context: Tags tell the browser whether a piece of text is a clickable button, a bold headline, or a plain sentence.
goals: See how tags turn text into interactive buttons
Assemble an element using the word bank

content.question: Which code snippet tells the browser to render a clickable button?

options.previewHtml: <button style='padding: 8px 18px; background: #f97316; color: white; border: none; border-radius: 8px; font-weight: 600; font-family: system-ui; cursor: pointer;'>Enroll Now</button>

content.explanation: The <button> tag signals to the browser's layout engine to create an interactive, clickable surface.

feedback.correct: Spot on. The <button> tags transform flat text into a clickable control.
feedback.incorrect: Plain text stays flat. Look for the snippet wrapped in opening and closing <button> tags.

content.prompt: Complete the opening tag using the Word Bank:

blanks.hint: What element creates an interactive button?

content.explanation: Opening tags start with <tag> and closing tags end with </tag>.

feedback.correct: Nice! <button> opens the tag, and </button> finishes it.
feedback.incorrect: Select 'button' from the Word Bank to complete the opening tag.

content.prompt: Arrange the pieces to build a complete button element:
content.explanation: HTML elements follow a sandwich pattern: Opening tag first, content in the middle, closing tag last.

feedback.correct: Clean sequence! Opening tag -> text -> closing tag.
feedback.incorrect: Remember the sandwich structure: <button> first, the text inside, and </button> at the end.

content.question: What character signals to the browser that a tag is closing?
content.explanation: A forward slash placed right after the angle bracket (</button>) flags the end of that element.

feedback.correct: Exactly. The forward slash marks the end of the tag.
feedback.incorrect: Check the closing tag: </button>. Notice the slash (/) directly preceding the tag name.

content.title: First Tag Mastered
takeaways: Tags wrap plain text to create real UI elements.
Opening tags look like <button>, and closing tags look like </button>.
The text goes between the tags like a sandwich.
nextSteps: Next up: Headings and Paragraphs — structuring text on a page.
